name: Crucible Shift Floor General Ops Uniform
description: The everyday uniform of a Crucible Industries general floor worker — not the specialized smelter or weld crew kits, but the backbone ops staff who keep materials moving, machinery logged, and shift quotas met. The jacket is a flame-resistant charcoal canvas work coat, thigh-length, with snap-off sleeves for hot-floor adaptability. The Crucible hex-and-anvil logo is heat-transfer printed across the upper back in dull orange. Chest pockets on both sides, one with a clear-window ID slot. Beneath it, a crew-neck work shirt in faded safety orange — washed to a muted clay tone after dozens of industrial cycles — with reinforced elbow patches in matching canvas. The shirt has a left-sleeve channel running from shoulder to wrist: an aug-accommodation track stitched into the seam to allow chrome arm hardware to sit flush without bunching fabric. Work trousers are heavy-gauge charcoal canvas with hammer loops, a full ring of tool eyelets at the waist, and double-stitched thighs. Boots are thick-soled composite safety boots with a puncture-resistant midsole and a self-tightening ankle strap. Safety goggles on an elastic band hang around the neck when not in use — scratched lenses, one replacement arm in a different color. A hardshell bump cap in safety orange sits low on the brow, often pushed back off the forehead by mid-shift.
functionality: Flame resistance for factory floor proximity, snap-off sleeves for temperature adaptability, aug-accommodation arm channel for chrome hardware, tool loops and hammer eyelets, puncture-resistant boot midsole, ID window pocket for floor access scanning, bump cap for overhead hazard zones.
what_it_says: Floor worker. Not management, not specialist crew — the kind of person who keeps the whole operation running while the supervisors take credit. The faded orange shirt means they've been here long enough to have laundered it thirty times. The scratched goggle lens means they don't expense replacements. There's no ego in this outfit, just hours.
price_range: Φ160–Φ210 (partially company-subsidized; workers cover 40% of cost)
story_hooks: A floor worker's ID window pocket holds two badges — their own and someone else's. One of them is for a section of the facility that doesn't appear on any public floor plan.
The snap-off sleeve modification on one jacket has been reversed and reinforced from the inside — someone has sewn something into the lining of that detachable sleeve.

A player needs to get onto a Crucible floor without credentials. The uniform is easy enough to find secondhand — but the bump cap color codes differ by section, and they don't know which color gets them to the right level.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian factory uniform that reads as pure function—blocky silhouette, layered protection, visual weight concentrated at the torso and feet. The wearer appears grounded, built for 12-hour shifts on a production floor. Dull orange and charcoal create a visual rhythm of safety protocol meeting industrial grime. The dangling goggles and repositioned bump cap suggest mid-shift fatigue and familiarity with the work.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and intentionally loose through the torso for movement and layering; structured at the shoulders from the work coat; tapered slightly at the ankles by the self-tightening boot straps. Sleeves designed for both removal and accommodation of chrome augmentation without compromise.
physical_description.primary_material: Flame-resistant charcoal canvas work coat and trousers; faded safety-orange crew-neck work shirt in reinforced synthetic cotton blend; composite safety boots with puncture-resistant polymer midsole; hardshell polycarbonate bump cap
physical_description.texture: Worn-soft canvas with subtle scuffing and heat-stress marks; reinforced patches feel thicker and stiffer; visible double-stitching at stress points; scratched, frosted goggles lens; self-tightening ankle strap has a tacky grip texture
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray as dominant; muted clay-orange (faded from safety orange) on shirt; bright dull orange accent on Crucible logo and bump cap; one mismatched goggles arm in a contrasting shade (possibly yellow or lime)
physical_description.closures: Snap fasteners on jacket sleeves for quick removal; traditional button-front on work shirt; cargo-style snap pockets on trousers; friction-fit self-tightening boot ankle strap; elastic goggles band
distinctive_features: Heat-transfer printed Crucible hex-and-anvil logo across upper back in dull orange
Left-sleeve aug-accommodation channel stitched into seam for flush chrome hardware integration
Full ring of tool eyelets at waist—multiple loops for hammer and wrench attachment
Clear-window ID slot on right chest pocket
Scratched and partially damaged safety goggles with mismatched replacement arm
Hardshell bump cap with wear marks and scuffing
Thick composite sole boots with visible tread wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 (working class, essential operations). The uniform signals neither wealth nor sub-grade desperation, but rather institutional stability and blue-collar necessity. Well-maintained but clearly worn.
physical_description.cultural_context: Factory floor operative, shift worker, Crucible Industries employee. The wearing of this uniform signals membership in the industrial backbone of the GLMZ—someone who keeps systems running. The aug-accommodation detail suggests familiarity with chrome and integration into corpo augmentation culture, but at the working level rather than executive tier. The mismatched goggles and pushed-back cap reveal personality within institutional constraint.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and worn, but not destroyed. Canvas shows heat-stress discoloration and minor fraying at edges; shirt is faded from countless washings; patches are clean and functional; boots show tread wear and minor scuff marks. The uniform reads as maintained equipment rather than salvage.
